title: Alameda County

# Alameda County

1,510,271 Total Population in 2010

In 2010, Alameda County was home to 1,510,271 people. Residents were predominantly working age, while those under 18 were a larger segment of the county than those 65 and older. The population was diverse, with no racial group in the majority.

## Sex and Age

In 2010, females outnumbered males by a moderate amount in Alameda County. Females 30-39 were the largest group by age, followed by females 40-49 and males 30-39. The biggest gap was in the 80-and-older age group, where females were the larger share.

## Race and Hispanic or Latino

34%

White (Not Hispanic or Latino)

In 2010, Alameda County had a diverse population with no race/ethnicity being a majority. White and Asian people were the largest groups in the county, while Hispanic and Black residents were the next biggest segments of the population.

### Population by Race and Hispanic or Latino

### Table: Population by Race and Hispanic or Latino

| Race and Hispanic or Latino | Population in Alameda County | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| | Total | Percentage |
| White | 514,559 | 34% |
| Black or African American | 184,126 | 12% |
| American Indian / Alaska Native | 4,189 | <1% |
| Asian | 390,524 | 26% |
| Native Hawaiian / Pacific Islander | 11,931 | <1% |
| Other / Multiracial | 65,053 | 4% |
| Hispanic or Latino (any race) | 339,889 | 23% |

* Categorized as Not Hispanic. This means that all the racial groups marked with an asterisk — White, Black or African American, American Indian / Alaska Native, Asian, Native Hawaiian / Pacific Islander, and Other / Multiracial — do not include individuals who identify as Hispanic or Latino. The "Hispanic or Latino (any race)" category is separate, as Hispanic/Latino is considered an ethnicity rather than a racial category. For the chart above, the data is collected from the U.S. Census Bureau Decennial Data 2010, Summary File 1 (SF1), P5 Hispanic or Latino Origin by Race.
